description:
The Rune Bolts are a power level 8 ammunition crafted at a Fletching Bench. Despite being power level 8, these bolts deal the same damage as adamant bolts.

[Journal] You may have wondered where the phrase 'out of the blue' or 'a bolt from the blue' comes from. Its origins are actually from Misthalin, from the humans who made their way through the mountains to Isafdar. On arrival, they would be ambushed by roving elves, some of whom would fire rune arrows and bolts. Elves are a stealthy bunch, so the first thing a human soldier might know about the ambush would be an arc of blue (the 'blue' being the rune metal). The soldiers would worry about being shot by 'a bolt from the blue', which is where the saying originated. Also see 'the thin blue line' and 'screaming blue murder'.

name: Rune Fire Arrow

description:
Rune fire arrows are a power level 8 ammunition that can be crafted with a fletching bench.

[Journal] The rune fire arrow is central to a story about the knight commander, Sir Leigh. In his will, Sir Leigh requested a full-boat burning. He wanted to be pushed out to sea, towards the mainland where he was born, and an archer was to set the pyre alight with a rune fire arrow. Sat at his desk, writing the will, it would have sounded like a fantastic idea to Sir Leigh. But in reality it was very different. Rune, you see, has repulsive properties. It is diamagnetic. So when Sir Leigh was laid to rest in his gold armour atop a raft, and the archer tried to aim for the pyre-wood beneath him, the rune arrows would not hit. Dozens upon dozens of arrows were fired, and they all deviated from their path thanks to the runic properties. By the time a boat was sent out with a man holding a lit torch, two seagulls and one shark had been set alight.

name: Steel Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips forged from Steel.

description:
Steel arrows are a power level 5 ammunition that are crafted at a fletching bench.

[Journal] Traditional wisdom says that to kill a zombie, you must destroy the brain. This is disappointingly untrue in Fellhollow, the animating force of Imaru’s hunger needs no thought to drive it forward. No, a far better plan is to destroy the bones and muscles with sharp metal-tipped spikes launched at the creatures with as much force as you can manage. Steel arrows perform this task very nicely.

name: Steel Barbed Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Lacerating arrows with barbed tips forged from Steel.

description:
Steel barbed arrows are power level 5 ammunition that can be created on the fletching bench.

[Journal] Sometimes it's not enough to just kill your enemy. There are times when you really want them to suffer as well. Steel arrows are nasty enough, but covering them in deadly barbs that will rend the flesh and empty the liquid lifeforce of a person onto the forest floor? That's just overkill.

name: Steel Bolts
description:
Steel bolts are a power level 5 ammunition crafted at a fletching bench.

[Journal] Sharpened bolts of steel projected at great speed is a formula for your target to have a very bad day. Although it was cheaper and quicker to forgo the coal and craft iron bolts, the relentless nature of the undead hordes required a more practical approach. Steel was stronger than iron, and was more likely to put the ravenous undead back in the dirt where they belonged, making it very popular in the last few years of Fellhollow’s resistance.

name: Steel Fire Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Burning arrows with tips forged from Steel coated in fire oil.

description:
Steel fire arrows are only accessible in the cache and are not present in the game.

[Journal] Some people just want to watch the world burn! Some people want to watch the world burn, but have thought through the logistics of fire and so decided to set the world aflame from a distance. These arrows are popular among the latter category.

name: Stone Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips of splintered stone.

description:
Stone arrows are power level 1 ammunition crafted at a Crafting Table.

[Journal] The Stone Arrow's weight and durability make it a more popular choice among hunters. The hardness of the tip makes it better at piercing tough animal hides or less durable forms of armour. In the Second Age, druids considered it a form of cheating, citing that it required a human's ingenuity to create rather than being a gift of nature. They seldom complained when the evening meal was served, celebrating the success of the hunt alongside everyone else. Even with somewhere as remote as Ashenfall, some humans turned to banditry, and they were very fond of Stone Arrows. Cheap and easy to produce, they help to kill and threaten anyone who makes the mistake of travelling through bandit-controlled woodland. One such bandit, the self-described 'bandit king, Otho', would choose only "interesting" stones to turn into arrows. Glittering pebbles that swished through the air. He was nicknamed the "Magpie King" because of his love for shiny pebbles. A moniker he was very unhappy with.
